sources.entry: Mataroa - Naked blogging platform for minimalists. (Source Code) MIT Python

summary.one_liner: Mataroa is a minimalist, subdomain-based blogging platform written in Django and PostgreSQL, with Caddy and gunicorn for deployment.
summary.what_it_does: Mataroa is a Django blogging platform where each user's blog is served on its own subdomain (username.domain). The main app, `main`, holds all business logic, covering posts, pages, comments, images, analytics, RSS feeds, newsletter subscriptions, and a webring. Blogs can be exported as Hugo, Zola, or epub archives, and posts can be imported. An API uses its own key-based authentication, and posting by email is supported through a Postmark inbound webhook. The README also describes moderation tooling for spam and campaign review, and a Stripe-based optional premium billing setup. Local development uses Docker Compose or uv with PostgreSQL, and a `devdata` command generates sample users and posts.
use_cases: run a multi-user blogging platform on subdomains
self-host a blog with email posting
export blog content to Hugo, Zola, or epub
set up a Django and PostgreSQL blog for development
notable: Subdomain-per-user blog hosting with Caddy handling automatic Let's Encrypt certificates
Blog export to Hugo, Zola, and epub formats
Strict, documented dependency policy with no third-party Django apps and no JavaScript libraries
Stores all content, including images, in PostgreSQL, which simplifies backup and migration
caveats: Local development requires editing /etc/hosts and adding an entry for each test user account
Optional Stripe billing and Postmark email setup need external accounts and extra configuration
Self-hosting requires DNS wildcard setup and a server provisioned with the included scripts
